tipo.cita: Single-centre, retrospective, observational convenience sample of patients diagnosed with melanoma at a tertiary care cancer hospital.

datos_origen.cita: Single-centre, retrospective, observational convenience sample of patients diagnosed with melanoma at a tertiary care cancer hospital.
3D-images were obtained as standard of care using VECTRA WB360 Whole Body 3-dimensional Imaging System (Canfield Scientific).
Automated data from image processing (i.e. lesion size, colour, border) for all eligible participants were exported from VECTRA DermaGraphix research software for analysis.

datos_tamano.cita: A total of 35 patients contributed 23,538 automatically identified skin lesions >2 mm in largest diameter (102-3021 lesions per participant).
There were 49 lesions of melanoma and 22,489 lesions that were not melanoma.

datos_pais.buscado: Se leyó entero el resumen (referencias/_texto-completo/marchetti-2023-resumen-pubmed.txt, líneas 5-13) y se buscaron nombres de país, ciudad o institución ('United States', 'USA', 'New York', 'Memorial', 'Sloan', 'MSKCC'): solo dice 'Single-centre' y 'a tertiary care cancer hospital' (línea 9), sin país. La ficha nombra MSKCC solo en una nota nuestra ('Dato de contexto', líneas 33-38), que no es texto del trabajo.

datos_unidad.cita: To determine if melanoma can be distinguished from other skin lesions using data from automated analysis of 3D-images.
There were 49 lesions of melanoma and 22,489 lesions that were not melanoma.
Considering all lesions in a patient-level analysis, 14 (28%) melanoma lesions had the highest predicted score or were in the 99th percentile among all lesions for an individual patient.

resultado_principal.cita: The AUC for the prediction model was 0.94 (95% CI: 0.92-0.96).
Considering all lesions in a patient-level analysis, 14 (28%) melanoma lesions had the highest predicted score or were in the 99th percentile among all lesions for an individual patient.

In this proof-of-concept pilot study, we demonstrated that automated analysis of whole-body 3D-images using simple image processing techniques can discriminate melanoma from other skin lesions with high accuracy.

contrastes.cita: Single-centre, retrospective, observational convenience sample of patients diagnosed with melanoma at a tertiary care cancer hospital.
Eligible participants were those with a whole-body 3D-image captured within 90 days prior to the diagnostic skin biopsy.
All were White patients and 23 (66%) were males.
23,538 automatically identified skin lesions >2 mm in largest diameter (102-3021 lesions per participant).

Existing artificial intelligence for melanoma detection has relied on analysing images of lesions of clinical interest, which may lead to missed melanomas. Tools analysing the entire skin surface are lacking.
Automated data from image processing (i.e. lesion size, colour, border) for all eligible participants were exported from VECTRA DermaGraphix research software for analysis.
To determine if melanoma can be distinguished from other skin lesions using data from automated analysis of 3D-images.
The main outcome was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
Considering all lesions in a patient-level analysis, 14 (28%) melanoma lesions had the highest predicted score or were in the 99th percentile among all lesions for an individual patient.
There were 49 lesions of melanoma and 22,489 lesions that were not melanoma.
